newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan's Dewan Salman down 3.15 pct.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan's Dewan Salman down 3.15 pct.

text.p: Shares of Dewan Salman Fibre fell 1.10 rupees, or 3.15 percent, to 33.80 on Sunday in response to reports that the government might cut duties on imported cotton and some types of synthetic fibre, dealers said.
A turnover of 2.105 million shares of Dewan Salman had been recorded at the Karachi bourse just before midday.
Caretaker Commerce Minister Zubair Khan said on Saturday that the government was considering revising duties on imports of raw cotton and synthetic fibres not produced in Pakistan.
The duty cuts are part of a relief package likely to be announced in the next few days aimed at helping the textile industry cope with a shortfall in domestic cotton production.
"The duty cuts may not directly hit local manufacturers of synthetic fibre, but will certainly lower demand," an analyst at KASB & Co said.
Pakistan's cotton output is expected to reach 9.2 to 9.5 million 375-lb bales in the 1996/97 (July-June) financial year, down from a target of 10 million bales and 9.96 million produced in 1995/96.
